title: Formal chain rule and invertible linear Jacobian for power-series parameters
statement: Let $F$ be a field, $n\ge0$, $T=F[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and let $y_1,\ldots,y_n$ be a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters] of $T$ such that the $F$-algebra homomorphism $F[[Y_1,\ldots,Y_n]]\to T$, $Y_k\mapsto y_k$, is an isomorphism; through it, $T=F[[y_1,\ldots,y_n]]$ and $\partial/\partial y_k$ denotes the termwise formal partial derivative in these coordinates, as $\partial/\partial x_i$ does in the original ones. Let $Q=(\partial y_k/\partial x_i)_{k,i}$ and $P=(\partial x_i/\partial y_k)_{i,k}$, $n\times n$ matrices over $T$ [def-weil-matrix]. Then: (1) for every $h\in T$ and every $i$, $\partial h/\partial x_i=\sum_{k=1}^n(\partial h/\partial y_k)(\partial y_k/\partial x_i)$, i.e. the row $(\partial h/\partial x_i)_i$ equals the row $(\partial h/\partial y_k)_k$ multiplied by $Q$; symmetrically $\partial h/\partial y_k=\sum_i(\partial h/\partial x_i)(\partial x_i/\partial y_k)$; (2) the matrix $Q(0)$ of constant terms of the entries of $Q$ (the linear coefficients of the $y_k$) is invertible over $F$; (3) $Q$ is invertible over $T$, with inverse $P$. The case $n=0$ (empty matrices) is included.
